Vancomycin should be avoided for routine use but may be needed if there is meticillin resistance. Ri- fampicin may be added in severe Staph. aureus infections. An oral fluoroquinolone such as ciprofloxacin may be used for Gram-negative infections.7 Intraperitoneal ceftazidime may be added in cases of pseudomonal infec- tion where resolution of infection is slow or where there is recurrence. Long-term antibacterial prophylaxis is not generally effec- tive, but Staph. aureus nasal carriage is associated with increased risk of exit-site infections and intranasal or exit- site mupirocin (cream, as ointment may damage the cath- eter) or exit-site gentamicin cream have been used to re- duce them.7 Dramatic reductions in peritonitis rates have been achieved with programmes based on stringent aseptic wound care and on minimising contact of the CAPD sys- tem with domestic water.8 1.
